# SquirrelSelect

> A stylesheet for the native HTML `<select>`. Add `class="sqs"` to a `<select>` and load one CSS file. No JavaScript, no wrapper component, no init call. Keyboard, screen readers, autofill and form validation stay with the browser.

Key facts:

- Package: `@3m5-de/squirrel-select`. Import `@3m5-de/squirrel-select/squirrel-select.css`, or link `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@3m5-de/squirrel-select@1/dist/squirrel-select.css`.
- One class: `sqs`. Optional classes: `sqs-icon` and `sqs-hint` inside options, `sqs-arrow-start` on the select.
- Customize with CSS variables named `--sqs-*`, set on the select or any ancestor. The stylesheet lives in the cascade layer `squirrel`, so any unlayered rule wins without `!important`.
- Dark mode follows the page: declare `color-scheme: light dark`.
- The open list is fully styled in Chrome and Edge 135+ and Safari 27+ with a mouse or trackpad. Firefox and older browsers show the system list with a styled field. Phones open the native picker on purpose.
- Every `<option>` needs visible text. Every select needs a visible `<label>`.
- Do not combine `sqs` with Bootstrap's `form-select` or similar classes.
- For list boxes use `multiple` with `size` of 4 or more. `multiple` with `size="1"` stays unstyled.
- No search, tags or remote options. An optional search module is planned.

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://3m5.github.io/squirrel-select/docs/quickstart.html): install, add the class, change a color
- [How it works](https://3m5.github.io/squirrel-select/docs/how-it-works.html): what each browser shows, and why
- [Theming](https://3m5.github.io/squirrel-select/docs/theming.html): where to set variables, own rules, arrow, recipes
- [CSS variables](https://3m5.github.io/squirrel-select/docs/variables.html): every variable with its default
- [Troubleshooting](https://3m5.github.io/squirrel-select/docs/troubleshooting.html): styles not applying, Tailwind, Sass, TypeScript
